meta.title: Ethos
meta.description: AbstractOS is a user-first operating system. Learn the principles that guide every decision we make — and our commitment to your freedom to choose.

ethos.title: Put the user first. <accent>Protect their right to choose.</accent>
ethos.quote: “The devices you own should be able to run the software you choose. The software you choose can be open or closed source — the choice is yours. It is not our job to decide or cast judgement; it's our job to protect your right to choose.”

principles.title: Six ideas that shape AbstractOS
principles.description: Our ethos is simple to say and hard to live up to. These are the principles we hold ourselves to.

items.title: User first — not user always right
items.body: Every decision starts with the person using the device. That means sometimes saying no to a feature so the whole experience stays clear, fast and dependable.

items.title: Approachable for everyone
items.body: We design for the average, non-technical person first. If your parents can set it up and love it, we have done our job.

items.title: Never at the expense of experts
items.body: Catering to newcomers does not mean limiting power users. A real Linux system, real terminal and real freedom are always one step away.

items.title: A first-class alternative
items.body: We aim to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Google, Apple and Microsoft — polished, consistent and ready for daily life on any device.

items.title: Freedom grows with us
items.body: As AbstractOS grows, we will invest in user freedom — including open-source firmware for devices, alongside closed options if you want them.

items.title: Built in the open
items.body: Our designs, roadmap and code live publicly on GitLab. Anyone can follow along, give feedback and contribute.

roadmap.title: Where we are headed
roadmap.description: Ethos only matters if it ships. Here is what we are building next, straight from our public roadmap.

alpha-0-1.title: Alpha 0.1
items: A desktop environment built on Wingpanel, LightDM, Gala and Dock
x64 and 32-bit images you can run in a virtual machine
A GTK 3 / GTK 4 theme for a consistent look
Marker (markdown notes), Register (text editor) and Review (quick file previews)
Vala Welder MVP and a documented Vala development process
CI/CD pipelines for AppImages and Alpine APKs, plus an Alpine repository

alpha-0-2.title: Alpha 0.2
items: ARM build process producing flashable .img files
A finished installer and a guided first-run experience
Testing pipelines for AbstractOS and Vala applications
Development guidelines for what makes an “AbstractOS application”

alpha-0-3.title: Alpha 0.3
items: ARM, x86 and 32-bit .img and .iso images for real hardware

meta.title: Download
meta.description: Download AbstractOS {version} “{codename}” for x64, 32-bit and ARM. Try it in a virtual machine or flash it to a USB drive.

download.title: Get <accent>AbstractOS</accent>
download.description: Free to download, free to use. Pick your architecture, then run it in a virtual machine or write it to a USB drive.

options.label: Download options
options.alphaWarning: AbstractOS is alpha software. Expect rough edges and missing features. We recommend trying it in a virtual machine before installing on hardware you rely on.

x64.title: 64-bit (x64)
x64.description: For most modern PCs and laptops, and for running in a virtual machine.

x86.title: 32-bit (x86)
x86.description: For older hardware and lightweight virtual machines.

arm64.title: ARM64
arm64.description: For phones, tablets and ARM single-board computers. Arriving with Alpha 0.2.

install.title: Up and running in three steps
install.description: Prefer a virtual machine? Point GNOME Boxes, VirtualBox or virt-manager at the image and you are done.
install.imageAlt: AbstractOS USB Disk Utility ready to write the image to a flash drive

steps.title: Download an image
steps.text: Choose the build for your architecture above and verify its SHA256 checksum.

steps.title: Write it to a USB drive
steps.text: Use the AbstractOS USB Disk Utility, or any image writer, to flash the .img to a drive of 8 GB or more.

steps.title: Boot and install
steps.text: Restart from the USB drive, try the live session, then erase and install — or partition it your way.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.description: AbstractOS is lightweight by design, but more headroom makes everything feel smoother.
